summary: QA auditor endorses competency-based approach but demands runtime kill-switches, immutable chain-of-custody records, prompt-injection defenses, and vendor sandbox notification windows for foundation model updates.

Brief comment asks FDA to require full-loop auditing of how clinician responses to AI outputs are used or dismissed, with reasons recorded.

Steward of an imaging dataset standard recommends machine-checkable, versioned documentation of benchmark datasets, kept separate from performance judgments, including data-origin declarations for synthetic data.

Neurosurgical society urges mandatory, independently governed, outcome-linked postmarket data systems for higher-risk GenAI devices, built on professional society registries, with FDA-CMS coordination.

Wearable maker asks FDA to treat informational non-directive consumer GenAI functions as non-devices or under enforcement discretion, reconcile with wellness policy, and regulate regardless of deployer.

Quality executive urges reversibility as a gating risk factor, criteria for meaningful human review, retained manufacturer accountability, prompt changes under change control, and targeted postmarket monitoring.

Promotional comment supporting competency-based evaluation, modular regulatory units, foundation model lineage and drift detection, and continuous telemetry, presenting the submitter's orchestration platform.

Clinician-educator recommends benchmarking sensitivity to claimed user seniority, testing real human override behavior, periodic re-credentialing-style re-examination, and MAFs disclosing refusal and stability behavior.

summary: Consultancy treats the two-axis framework as a screening tool, proposes adaptive user-comprehension as a risk control, flexible clinical confirmation, and SOUP-style controls for foundation models.
